insights: Promoting long-form content in Shorts causes severe abandonment: directing viewers to 'The full breakdown is on our channel' triggered a massive 24.1% audience drop-off at 38.6s.

Shorts reliably drive discovery over long-form: 5 of 8 Shorts crossed 1,000 views (averaging ~850 views), while 2 of the 3 long-form videos struggled below 50 views (note: 3 long-form videos is a very small sample size).
Subscriber acquisition is heavily concentrated in breakthrough tech/futuristic news: Quantinuum (+4), Tesla Roadster (+4), and Cell Aging (+3) generated 11 of the channel's 12 total subscribers.
Viewer interaction is critically low across all formats: only 2 comments were generated across all 11 videos combined, confirming end-of-video questions or prompts are failing to trigger replies.

Retention does not guarantee reach if the Shorts feed algorithm is missed: 'Nuclear Submarines' had the highest retention (78.01% AVP) but only reached 48 views because only 6% came from the Shorts feed.
Specific, high-stakes numbers in titles dramatically boost long-form clicks: adding 'at 2,000°C' to the Jet Engines title saw views jump from 4 to 410, though view percentage remained low (~24%).
Countdown and news formats achieve the strongest Shorts retention (64%–69% AVP), whereas question/explainer hooks saw heavy drop-offs within the first 7 seconds (e.g., Icebergs lost 9.0% at 6.9s).
